title: introduce-load-synthesizer-and-frugal-profile-builder
author: Claire Huang
release_notes: Added a synthetic load prober and conservative profile builder to generate safe batching/caching defaults and quantization presets; feature is opt-in behind feature flag; integrates with Optimize telemetry and defaults compiler.
description:
Background and motivation:
We need a lightweight, conservative way to produce tenant-specific defaults for batching, KV prefix caching, and quantization that protect latency SLOs while improving unit economics. Existing autotuners are strong for long-running signals but struggle with low-traffic tenants and cold-start patterns. This PR introduces two pieces: a load synthesizer that generates small, realistic synthetic traces for short-lived tenants and edge workloads, and a frugal-profile-builder that composes conservative batching/caching/quant presets from those traces plus historical telemetry. Both are opt-in and intended to bootstrap defaults before heavier sampling/autotuning finishes.

What this PR does (summary):
- Add tools/load_synthesizer: a small Python-based trace generator that produces distributional samples (seq_len, inter-arrival, skew) from either live telemetry or template profiles. It ships with three templates (burst, sparse, chatty-edge).
- Add optimizer/frugal_profile_builder: a controller that runs unit-econ micro-simulations on synthesized traces to produce safe profiles (batch size targets, max_wait_ms, cache_prefix_hit_thresholds, quantization profile suggestions with fallbacks).
- Wire the frugal-profile-builder into defaults-compiler as an opt-in source with a priority below long-running autotuners.
- Expose a CLI: redwoodctl profiles synth --tenant-id / --template to run locally and preview candidate defaults.
- Add telemetry hooks and a small set of metrics (synth_runs_total, profile_suggestions_total, profile_applied, simulated_token_cost_change) for Optimize and Console dashboards.
- Add unit and integration tests, microbenchmarks, and a smoke canary for rollout.

review_conversation:
Aisha Patel: Please add a metric that reports the simulated tail-latency distribution used for decision thresholds so we can reason about SLO trade-offs.
Claire Huang: Added simulated_tail_latency_p50_p95_p99 as a single histogram metric exposed by the simulator; updated metrics.yml and added dashboard seed.
Mateo Rivera: Integration looks good, but defaults-compiler priority needs clearer semantics — what happens if an autotuner later produces a conflicting profile?
Claire Huang: frugal profiles are written with source=frugal and priority=low; defaults-compiler will prefer higher-priority sources and the frugal profile is treated as a bootstrap that can be replaced. Added comments and a test to validate override semantics.
Jinsoo Park: CI flagged bench regression in simulator for large templates (burst).
Claire Huang: Fixed a pathological loop in the simulator sampling and added a micro-optimizing caching layer; re-ran bench -> CI passes.
Aisha Patel: Approve after tests pass.
Mateo Rivera: Approved.
Merge maintainer (ops): Squash-and-merge after CI green and feature flag added.
ci_checks: Initial CI: lint (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-tests (fail) -> fixed and rerun, bench-smoke (pass), e2e-canary (pass). Final status: all checks passed.
notes_on_rollout: Feature behind feature.frugal_profiles. Rollout plan: enable for internal tenants in canary region (us-west-2) for 48h, monitor simulated_token_cost_change and profile_applied, then expand to 10% of tenants. If simulated_token_cost_change shows >10% cost increase or profile_applied < 50% revert feature flag. Dashboard seeds included.
post_merge_tasks: (1) Add frugal profile explainer to support playbooks, (2) run migration to mark existing tenant defaults with source=fallback where appropriate, (3) schedule a telemetry alert to catch unexpected tail-latency increases.
security_considerations: No secrets added. CLI preview uses sanitized telemetry; frugal builder runs with read-only telemetry scopes. Documented required RBAC for running synth locally.
perf_impact_summary: Microbench added; baseline microbench shows ~0.8ms median overhead for a single simulation run per tenant when run in control-plane. Frugal profiles reduce simulated token cost by median 7% for sparse templates and up to 28% for chatty-edge templates in our synthetic experiments.
tests_and_benchmarks: Unit tests for simulator determinism and safety, integration test covering defaults-compiler override behavior, bench micro-run included in CI. Bench results attached in artifacts (bench/frugal_profile_microbench/2026-02-22).
